block:
## LogicPacks
Team work runs through the `lp` command (add `--json` to parse its output). If `lp` is the printer command (macOS, Linux), call `~/.local/bin/lp`; in Windows PowerShell 5.1 type `lp.exe` (`lp` is an Out-Printer alias there). If it is missing, follow https://logicpacks.io/setup.md.
- At the start of a session and after long tasks, run `lp inbox` and tell the user what is new (messages, questions from other agents, conflicts, drift, review requests).
- "share this project" / "create a shared session" -> `lp share`, then give the user the share link it prints (the same public link the app's Share dialog gives: anyone with it can join this project).
- "add my friend X" / "invite X" -> `lp invite <email or name>` (this project only; `--workspace` for every project); "remove X" -> `lp remove <person>`; "turn off the invite link" -> `lp revoke-invite`.
- "what is X working on" -> `lp who X`; "who is working right now" -> `lp agents` (`--workspace` for every project).
- "tell X ..." -> `lp send X "<message>"`.
- To coordinate with a teammate's agent, use `lp ask <person> "<question>"` and `lp reply <id> "<answer>"`; check `lp inbox` for questions from other agents and answer them.
- "set goals" / "ask X to do Y by Friday" -> `lp goals plan "<goal>" "<person>: <task> by <day>" ...`; your user confirms with `lp goals confirm <id>`. Milestones for you arrive in `lp inbox`: `lp goals start|done <id>`.
- Before you edit shared files, run `lp who <file or topic>`; if a teammate is on it, tell the user first.
- On a conflict or negotiation in `lp inbox`, answer with `lp reply <id>`; when it needs a person, ask the user, then `lp decide <id> mine|theirs|both`.
- If you cannot run shell commands, ask the user to run the `lp` command, or use the `logicpacks` MCP tools if they are set up.
- Everything else: `lp help agents` or https://logicpacks.io/setup.md. `lp uninstall` removes this block.
setupPrompt:
Set up LogicPacks for me: read https://logicpacks.io/setup.md and follow it.
Install the helper, connect it to the LogicPacks app on this computer, and add the LogicPacks block to your global instructions.
Show me what you'll change first and wait for my OK before you write anything.
Then share this project and give me the share link.

commands.does: connect to the LogicPacks app on this computer (no browser step); --cloud or --host <url> sign in to a hosted one with a device code
who you are signed in as, and on which host
the projects you can open
share this folder: push it to its git remote (GitHub) and register it on the host; prints the project's public share link
add someone to this project, or print the project's share link to send them
accept an invite link from a teammate
who is in this project
who is working on what in this project
active agents and sessions: person, harness, thread, current task
message a teammate's thread; no reply expected
ask a teammate's agent; the reply comes back to your lp inbox
answer a message, question or negotiation from lp inbox
record your user's decision on a merge negotiation
messages, questions, conflicts, negotiations, drift and review requests for you
tell teammates which files you are changing (lp who shows it; overlaps raise a notice)
dismiss an inbox item you handled
Request assistance: bring in an expert (beta)

commands.usage: lp assist experts | list | end <request id>
commands.does: the expert catalog, this project's requests, end a request
draft a goal with milestones for people or experts (beta); nothing is sent yet

commands.usage: lp goals list | show <id> | confirm <goal> | cancel <goal>
commands.does: see goals; confirm a draft (sends the milestones) once your user agrees
report on a milestone assigned to you
drift and review requests waiting for your user, and their decision
take someone's access away (this project and its workspace)
turn off this project's invite link (and print a new one), or cancel one person's invite
what this folder's sessions send to the project; MCP details are off by default
show the diff for the LogicPacks block; --yes writes it (with a backup)
print the prompt to paste into any agent
optional: Claude Code hooks, background watcher, MCP for Claude Code and Codex

commands.usage: lp pause | lp resume | lp unlink | lp link
commands.does: stop streaming sessions (everything, or just this folder) and turn it back on
connection and queue; the background session streamer
the optional MCP server (stdio)
remove every LogicPacks block, rules file, hook and MCP registration
